(We're 3)
summary: Our challenge was to design and develop an intuitive lunar landing site navigator for future NASA space missions on the south pole of the moon. Our goal was to create a tool that would make it easy to compare different NASA lunar landing sites at different times. Mission times are particularly difficult to plan, as mission planning rarely follows a neat timeline. To address this, our tool provides a clear 1-to-10 suitability score based on critical operational factors, including solar irradiance, local terrain topology, and direct-line-of-sight communications with Earth. This score, which is based on the date and time inputed by the users, enables mission planners to rapidly compare candidate sites and evaluate potential launch windows. By automating complex underlying calculations, this tool makes it efficient for the user to decide which landing site is the best. It's important to be able to make this decision quickly and easily to better prepare for the upcoming space missions.
details:
Our team created a user-friendly application designed to score different potential landing locations across different timeframes. The underlying computations were developed using Python, while Unity was used to code the interface the user interacts with. The python libraries we used for this project include Skyfield, which handles complex astrophysical calculations like solar elevation, surface irradiance on the moon, and direct Earth communication paths. Additionally, the rasterio module was essential for processing GeoTIFF datasets, allowing us to perform accurate slope calculations and surface coordinate mapping across the moon.

The primary function of our app was to provide users with an intuitive landing rating for a selected location and time. However, if given additional time to code, several other added features were planned, such as:

- Side-by-side windows for comparing different sites and times;

- A score that indicates the amount of fuel needed to land on the site based on orbital calculations;

- An interactive, fully animated lunar cartographic view;

- A score that considers how the topology of the land creates shadows that limit irradiance

- The ability to input any lunar coordinate instead of picking from a handful of predetermined candidates

- Dynamic timelines to visualize site evolution;

- Settings that allow the user to change the weight importance of each criteria

Despite the tight 48-hour hackathon timeframe, we strove to integrate as many innovative and creative features as possible into our space application.  The intended impact of comparing different landing sites is still up and working in our project, which will hopefully help mission planners with future lunar endeavours and will provide valuable decision support. :)
